explanation: Mozart is famous for dying young, at 35, but Schubert died at 31, having written more than 600 songs. He was a torchbearer at Beethoven's funeral the year before.

claims.text: Schubert was a torchbearer at Beethoven's funeral in 1827, the year before his own death.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: clean under content:check for writer w-pmusic01w. Claims: every checkable statement in the stem, options and explanation is listed, with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a fact is beyond everyday knowledge. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers these music facts (the manifest holds geographic, scientific, Nobel, Olympic and art-collection data), so each high-risk claim needs web evidence from the checkers. I used no WebSearch. Rival test: argued for Schubert: Mozart is the textbook composer who died young, so most players will assume anyone else lived longer, which is the trap; Mozart (1756 to 1791) reached 35 and Schubert (1797 to 1828) 31. The ratio of 35 to 31 passes the 1.1 guard. Volatility: evergreen; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: both composers are known worldwide, and the trap rests on Mozart's global fame. Style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words. Myths: screened against myths.json, no hit. Mystery: not applicable to a practice item. Encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: None of substance; both ages follow from undisputed birth and death dates.
